Count observations by group

Source: R/count.R
count.tbl_gpu.Rd

Counts the number of rows (or sums a weight column) for each combination of ..., similar to dplyr::count(). Sugar over group_by.tbl_gpu(), summarise.tbl_gpu(), and arrange.tbl_gpu() – runs on the GPU. The one exception is a .drop = FALSE grouping with a factor key, or a table with fixed group keys (after filter(), semi_join(), ... on a .drop = FALSE table), which also collects the (small) group keys to add the empty groups.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'tbl_gpu'
count(
  x,
  ...,
  wt = NULL,
  sort = FALSE,
  name = NULL,
  .drop = dplyr::group_by_drop_default(x)
)

Arguments

x

A tbl_gpu object created by tbl_gpu().

...

Column names or expressions to group by (e.g. count(df, x) or count(df, g = x %/% 10)), parsed through the same expression IR mutate.tbl_gpu() uses for any computed expression. If x is already grouped, these are added to the existing grouping (matching group_by(x, ..., .add = TRUE)).

wt

Optional weight column/expression. If supplied, each group's count is sum(wt) (NA-excluding) instead of the row count.

sort

If TRUE, sorts the result in descending order of the count column.

name

The name of the count column in the output. If NULL (default), uses "n", or "nn"/"nnn"/... if "n" already names one of the (post-...) grouping columns.

.drop

Passed to group_by.tbl_gpu(); with .drop = FALSE the result has a zero-count row for every empty factor-level group, in group_data() order. Defaults to group_by_drop_default(x).

Value

A tbl_gpu object with one row per group, containing the grouping columns and the count column. Grouping: if x was ungrouped, the result is ungrouped; if x was grouped, the result's grouping is restored to x's ORIGINAL grouping in full (verified against dplyr 1.2.1 – see this file's header comment for why this is not simply "drop the last grouping level").

See also

tally.tbl_gpu, group_by.tbl_gpu, summarise.tbl_gpu

Examples

library(dplyr)
if (has_gpu()) {
  gpu_mtcars <- tbl_gpu(mtcars)
  gpu_mtcars |> count(cyl) |> collect()
  gpu_mtcars |> count(cyl, sort = TRUE) |> collect()
}
#>   cyl  n
#> 1   8 14
#> 2   4 11
#> 3   6  7
